theorem.summary: On an original-coordinate core H, split an arbitrary signed spectral addition E into favorable and hostile sign parts. Any chosen hostile modes cost only the dimension of their projected footprint span. The remaining hostile modes cost their exact overlap-weighted local spectral mass sum |theta_a| ||P_H v_a||^2 divided by the number of unused reserve directions. This yields signed eigenvalue lower bounds for the actual final physical core and hence a dependence-safe density bound by conditioning outside H.

exact_family.global_target_check: principal interlacing gives at least two positive and one negative full-matrix eigenvalues of modulus >=7/2

unresolved_implication: From bare s3(A)>=1, force a bounded original-coordinate core with enough signed reserve and either low hostile projected-footprint rank or small hostile overlap-weighted spectral mass, or route failure exhaustively into the already-paid volume/ridge/hub/pair/Schur branches.
next_step: Test the local spectral-mass currencies against the current concentrated-volume/no-pivot survivors, especially whether a heavy spectral packet necessarily has either low projected footprint dimension on a bounded core or enough diffuse overlap to trigger an existing volume/projected-crossing exit.
